rubric.evidence: The whatwg/html PR #11980 has MERGED since the page was first written; all spec claims now cite the canonical HTML Standard section (media.html#attr-media-loading) and the lazy-loading-attributes section (urls-and-fetching.html#lazy-loading-attributes), both fetched 2026-08-09. The IDL line ([CEReactions] attribute DOMString loading; on HTMLMediaElement) and the reflection sentence ('limited to only known values') were extracted verbatim from the fetched spec HTML. The eager-switch resumption steps (lazy load resumption steps + poster resumption steps for video) trace to the state-change algorithm in the same section. The runtime flag LazyLoadVideoAndAudio (now status: stable) was verified in runtime_enabled_features.json5; the crbug 514611050 partial-support note comes from BCD's own note field.

Feature id 5200068565139456 verified present in features_by_type for milestone=147 under 'In developer trial (Behind a flag)' (live listing fetched 2026-08-09), so the v147 placement and dev-trial framing remain correct. The page now also states the shipped timeline honestly: partial 148-149, full 150 (BCD), so a reader landing on the v147 page is not misled into thinking the feature is still flag-gated.

Surface is small and fully covered: the content attribute (keywords, states, missing/invalid defaults), the IDL reflection, lifecycle (deferral, eager switch, preload/autoplay/play() interactions), examples, per-version compat, specifications, and security/privacy. reference-contract.json maps both inventory items across all nine dimensions to fragment anchors on this page. Not implementation-sufficient in the deepest sense of documenting Chromium's distance thresholds, which are deliberately browser-defined and unspecified - stated as such with the spec cited.

Keeps the original page's clear 'why it exists' narrative; adds a keywords/states table, an explicit invalid-values paragraph, and a lifecycle table that separates deferral, eager-switch, preload, autoplay, and play() interactions instead of one mixed table.

Four code examples retained/improved (detection now names HTMLMediaElement.prototype, where the IDL attribute actually lives) plus the live chrome-platform-showcase scroll-detector demo embedded as an iframe (route HEAD-checked 200 on 2026-08-09; loading=lazy, title present, var(--border-black) border).

Hand-written four-row 'browser support' table replaced by a real per-version BCD table (html.elements.video.loading / audio.loading): Chrome 150 full with 148-149 partial (crbug 514611050 linked), Chrome Android and Edge 150 via BCD mirror cross-checked against webstatus.dev dates, Firefox/Safari not-supported rows with their tracking bugs and standards positions linked. Baseline banner states 'Limited availability' per webstatus.dev loading-lazy-media - no implied cross-browser support.

Every previously-unlinked citation label now links directly to its artifact (chromestatus record, merged spec sections, BCD source files, webstatus.dev record, runtime_enabled_features.json5, both standards-position issues, crbug). All external links target=_blank rel=noopener.
Baseline banner uses role=note with aria-label; iframe has a descriptive title; tables carry captions and th scope attributes; single h1; heading order h1>h2>h3 preserved.

All tables wrapped in .table-wrap (overflow-x auto) with overflow-wrap:anywhere cells per the shared pattern; no fixed min-widths. Matrix run recorded in responsive-support.json for this route (screenshots read).

The page now embeds this feature's own chrome-platform-showcase scroll-detector concept (200) and links all five live concept routes in see-also; the stale '(when built)' placeholder text was removed.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive data table horizontal scroll small screens
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Keep wide data tables inside their own horizontally scrollable container and let cell content wrap (overflow-wrap) instead of forcing fixed table widths; size to content with intrinsic layout.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Wide reference tables stay in .table-wrap{overflow-x:auto} containers with overflow-wrap:anywhere cells so the page body never scrolls horizontally on 360px viewports; no fixed table min-widths.

guidanceConsulted.query: iframe embed lazy loading accessibility title
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Iframes need descriptive accessible names (title); use landmark roles/aria-labels for status callouts; tables need caption and th scope for screen-reader traversal.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The showcase iframe carries a descriptive title attribute and loading=lazy; the Baseline banner is a role=note landmark with an aria-label; compat/lifecycle tables use caption + th scope.

guidanceConsulted.query: lazy loading below the fold resources
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Defer below-the-fold embeds with loading=lazy so they do not compete with critical resources; keep LCP-critical content eager.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: The embedded demo iframe itself uses loading=lazy (below the fold), which is also the very pattern the documented feature extends to media elements.

openQuestions: Chromium's lazy-load distance thresholds for media are browser-defined; if Chromium publishes concrete threshold values for media elements (as it did for images), the Behavior section should cite them.
MDN does not yet document loading on video/audio; when MDN pages appear, re-evaluate whether this page should become a Case A stub (BCD keys exist already, so MDN coverage is likely coming).

followUpGoals.goal: Re-check html.elements.video.loading / audio.loading BCD quarterly and update the compat table when Firefox (bugzil.la/2005072) or Safari (webkit.org/b/303995) ship.
When MDN publishes reference pages for media loading attributes, decide stub-vs-full per CLAUDE.md invariant #6 and cross-link.
Add a note on interaction with poster lazy-loading on <video poster> once Chromium's poster deferral behavior is observable in stable (spec already defines poster resumption steps).
